steps.name: Prepare ranked gene list from DESeq2 results
caveats: sample_01 has ~4x below-median library size; this affects the upstream DE estimates being consumed here, not this step's ranking logic itself
Confirm the exact column names in de_results.csv before scripting (gene, log2_fold_change, and the p-value/stat columns) since the profile lists 8 columns but only names the first few
steps.context: Input is /eval-full-32-without-enrichment-only-ranked-1/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, a DESeq2 results table (12000 x 8: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2fc-related SE/stat, pvalue, padj columns) for the treated (psoriasis lesional) vs control skin contrast, 6 vs 6 unpaired design.
steps.question: How should the 12000-gene DESeq2 treated-vs-control results table (gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2fc SE/stat, p-value, padj) be converted into a single ranking metric per gene for pre-ranked GSEA?
acceptance_criteria: Output is a two-column table (gene symbol, rank statistic) covering all genes in de_results.csv with non-missing p-value and log2FC
Ranking metric is signed by direction of change (sign of log2_fold_change) and monotonic in significance (e.g. -log10(pvalue) or the DESeq2 Wald/stat column if present)
Duplicate or missing gene symbols are resolved/dropped and reported (count removed)
Report explicitly notes the sample_01 low-library-size caveat as a known limitation of the upstream DE result being consumed, not re-analyzed

steps.name: Pre-ranked GSEA against MSigDB hallmark gene sets
caveats: Hallmark sets are broad/curated composite states, not fine-grained pathways; report set name exactly as HALLMARK_* without renaming
Gene symbol matching between de_results.csv and the GMT may drop unmapped genes; report the match rate
steps.context: Reference: the MSigDB human hallmark gene set collection (50 sets, HALLMARK_* names, HGNC gene symbols, GMT format) staged in this environment for Homo sapiens, matching the skin/psoriasis dataset's organism.
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB hallmark pathways are significantly enriched (up or down) in psoriasis lesional vs control skin, based on the ranked DESeq2 gene list?
acceptance_criteria: Runs pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea or gseapy prerank) using the ranked list from T1S1 against the human MSigDB hallmark GMT (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols)
Reports NES, p-value, and BH-adjusted q-value (FDR) per hallmark pathway, sorted by adjusted p-value
Explicitly labels which pathways are enriched in treated (positive NES/up in lesional) vs control (negative NES) directions
Uses standard GSEA parameters (e.g. 1000+ permutations or fgsea's default multilevel exact test) and reports gene-set size filters applied (e.g. min 15, max 500 genes matched)
If the hallmark GMT is unavailable at run time, the step reports this explicitly and does not fabricate pathway results

steps.name: Overrepresentation analysis on significant DE genes vs hallmark sets
caveats: ORA is sensitive to the padj<0.05 cutoff choice; report how many genes pass and whether the list is large enough (>=10-15) for meaningful hypergeometric testing
Background universe should be the 12000 genes present in de_results.csv, not a genome-wide default, to avoid inflated significance
steps.context: Same DESeq2 results table and MSigDB human hallmark GMT as T2S1; this step uses a hard significance threshold rather than the full ranked list, as an independent, simpler check on the GSEA result.
steps.question: Among genes significantly changed (padj < 0.05) between psoriasis lesional and control skin, which hallmark pathways are overrepresented, and do results corroborate the pre-ranked GSEA (T2S1)?
acceptance_criteria: Defines a significant gene list from de_results.csv using padj < 0.05 (and reports the resulting gene count, split up- vs down-regulated by log2_fold_change sign)
Runs hypergeometric/Fisher ORA against the MSigDB human hallmark gene sets with all 12000 profiled genes as the background universe
Reports odds ratio/enrichment score, raw p-value, and BH-adjusted q-value per hallmark pathway
Cross-references top hits against the T2S1 pre-ranked GSEA results and flags any pathway significant in one method but not the other
If de_results.csv column names differ from assumed padj/log2_fold_change naming, script adapts to actual header and reports the mapping used

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: DESeq2 DE results for the psoriasis lesional vs control skin contrast (12000 genes, 6 vs 6, single batch) are already computed in de_results.csv. The research question asks specifically which MSigDB hallmark pathways change between conditions. The environment carries the MSigDB human hallmark GMT (50 sets, HGNC symbols) matching the human/skin organism of this dataset. Rather than re-deriving DE, the plan takes the existing DESeq2 statistics table directly into a pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea-style) against the hallmark collection, ranking genes by a signed statistic (e.g. sign(log2FC)*-log10(p) or the Wald stat if present) to get directional NES per hallmark pathway. A companion step also runs classic overrepresentation (ORA) on genes passing a significance threshold, to cross-check the ranked result and give a simpler, threshold-based readout. The sample_01 library-size caveat is noted for the report but does not require re-running DE since results are supplied, not derived here.
